title: Wall Art Made by Mansi
medium: Ink and natural pigment on wall

title: Fish of the Mithila River
medium: Ink and natural pigment on handmade paper
description: Two fish circle each other in a river of double lines — a classic Mithila motif for fertility and abundance. The border is drawn freehand with a bamboo nib, then filled with pigment made from lamp soot and indigo.

title: Harvest Circle
description: A Warli tarpa dance drawn in white rice paste on earth-red ground. The figures join hands in an unbroken circle — in Warli cosmology the dance keeps the world turning. Every triangle is a body, every line a shared breath.

title: Kalamkari Peacock
description: A peacock drawn with a kalam (bamboo pen) and dyed with myrobalan, iron rust and madder root. The palette comes entirely from minerals and plants — no synthetic colour touches this cloth.

title: Lotus Pond at Dusk
description: Pichwai-inspired lotus pond painted with stone colours and finished with fine gold detail. The lotus opens at dusk, when the pond turns the colour of old brass.

title: Bird of the Sal Forest
description: A Gond bird built from dots and dashes, the way the Gond artists of central India fill every creature with pattern. The bird carries the forest inside it.

title: A Morning with Natural Dyes
description: A short film following one morning in the studio: boiling pomegranate rind, straining indigo, and painting the first wash onto paper. Filmed and edited by the artist. Sound on for the birds outside the window.
